title: The Circumference of Truth and Divine Light
english: He does not use mere words, but promises an unchangeable and unalterable will. Since his will regarding the man from David becoming his son is unalterable, it is fitting that the Lord said to my servant, 'You are my son' (Ps 88:7). No one of those born from God, having received the spirit of adoption, will be able to become like the Lord. For he alone, according to truth, is the offspring of God, while the others are called sons of God to partake in him.

For the sake of a perfect understanding of what is set forth, we shall use the apostolic voice, which sounds thus: 'Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ' (2 Cor 13:14). For having called God Father of himself and of those near him, he was reverent, not assigning to himself an equality with any glory to the only-begotten Son; therefore he added, 'And the Lord Jesus Christ,' having cried out only once: 'if indeed we have become sons by the grace of God, and he himself becomes our Father, yet also we are slaves of Jesus Christ according to the nature of our Lord who is' (Rom 8:17).

This very thought is confirmed by the set-forth word: 'For who shall be like the Lord among the sons of God?' (Exod 35:19). No one is, according to essence, a son of God, except the Savior alone, who is the only one consubstantial with the Father; but those who are not according to essence, but according to quality, shall be made like him, just as they become merciful like the Father and perfect as the Father becomes: 'You shall be holy, because I am holy' (Lev 11:44). For the Lord comes upon the clouds of heaven with much power and glory, and the saints shall be caught up in clouds to meet the Lord in the air, to be with him forever (1 Thess 4:17).

Therefore, of the Lord and the saints being in the clouds, no one of those caught up in clouds shall be equal to the one coming upon the clouds of heaven with much power and glory. For each one was caught up with power, but not with much glory. For that power and glory he possessed, but the Savior will come with much power and glory; and each of those was in a cloud, but not upon the clouds. The expression 'upon the clouds' establishes the authoritative and kingly, whence no one in clouds shall be equal to the Lord; for truly, the cloud of each of the saints, being spiritual, is the intelligible moisture (the clouds...

For he says, 'justice has overwhelmed' (Ps 88:8), no such clouds can be found equal to the Lord, who is also a cloud, since each of them only waters a little, but He waters not only all men but also all rational things.

He is also fearful to those who are opposed, threatening punishments and bringing them down against those who fall away from His divine commands. For you, being near Him in receiving His divine teaching, while sinning, are near the fire, as the words of the Savior say: 'He who is near me is near the fire, and he who is far from me is far from the kingdom.' Thus, in the present word, He is fearful to those around Him who, through having believed in Him, disobey His commandments; how great [is He] to those held by His virtue.

The truth about God is none other than the one saying, 'I am the truth' (John 14:6). If it is around God, it can never not be, lest God should descend from not being once surrounded by truth to this. But it is surrounded by this, generating it, and He alone is the true God. For just as He alone is wise, not participating in wisdom but generating wisdom, so He alone is true and has truth around Him, not taking part in it but being with others and giving it to them.

For the Father exists with the Son in every thought and energy; for the Word, being with God, is God the Word, since the Father is in the Son and the Son is in the Father; for it is fitting for a God-Word to be with God the Father. But also as light, God has light with Him, the Son, as it is said in Daniel: 'And the light is with Him.' For it is not 'was' or 'will be' but 'is,' for this shows eternity, and thus it is said to be an emanation of eternal light. And the truth is said not to have 'become' or 'be going to be' around, but to 'be' of the almighty God. And the eternal power will be present to the almighty God, which exists the same as the wisdom, truth, light, and Word of God, but also 'your truth is around you.'

Understand this (Ps 88:10): faith in Him ruling all creation and the sea, regarding what is written about Jonah; for there it is said that waves were stirred up in the sea, and again, the sea will be to Him from the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Creative Power and the Arm of God
english: of its violence. And Jesus, demonstrating by word what kind of son he is of the master of the dominion of the sea, rebukes it while it is being agitated and stirring up a storm, and immediately calms it.

But if the sea's allegory signifies the life of men, its dominion may be the evil one in whom the whole world lies, that is, the mortal and perilous state. By this, the master of the sea, providing weakness to its dominion, grants authority to the travelers to suffer against all his power, calming the unstable and irregular surges of its waves, which are called upon it, making it also a firm footing for those receiving authority to walk upon it with Jesus, of whom Peter bears the image.

For no one, apart from Jesus, is able to suffer the sea of life, becoming subject to anxieties and pleasant passions, unless he walks along with Jesus. For he is the one walking as if on dry land upon the sea, as it was said to him: 'Your ways, O God, are in the sea, and your paths in many waters' (Ps 88:12-13). For Jesus has trodden paths in the strong waters; the passions are also life-related anxieties that those following his tracks are able to mount.

Regarding the thought, all those interpreting confess his wonders, and the earth receiving Jesus, being a seed and bearing fruit, becomes his property, reaching one hundred and sixty and thirty. And he established the inhabited world upon its fullness, being no other than the church, in which souls dwell having adhered to the right reason and the truth. But sacred powers also dwell in it, intervening around those fearing him.

And the foundation upon which it was established is not other than that about which Paul writes, for no one else is able to lay a foundation other than the one laid, which is Jesus Christ. And the fullness of this spiritual inhabited world, being founded upon the same foundation, is the fullness of virtues and of the dogmas of piety, along with the divine gifts of the Spirit.
And the Lord created the north and the seas, so that they are no longer as they were before. For just as having created the two into one, a new man from the two, he has...

It has been struck, and the being-created heart is pure, from which it has become pure; and he creates also those outside of faith, so that in Christ they might become a new creation—not by creating the north wind and the seas. But everyone who obtains divine election and is suspended by light, having been enlightened, rejoices in the name of God with a light of knowledge.

Just as Tabor is indeed outside, but Hermonius is a suspension of light; for the Hebrew names of the mountains are taken toward these things. And if Tabor is also interpreted as a pit (for it does not carry the sense), you will understand how it is said 'a praiseworthy pit', having understood how God gives to some in a manner of blessing pits that have been dug; those who have dug them did not dig them out. And if the pit were spoken of in mockery, having changed the voice, it would not be named thus, as one should not enrich wells; the spring will rejoice upon the name of the Lord (Ps 88:14-15).

The poetic power of God (but this is His creative power, His only-begotten Son) is signified to all those who are within by name. For 'arms' is said in the [Psalms]: 'And the arm of the Lord, to whom was it revealed? And your arm, O Most High, and you shall not be afraid.' But also the 'hand of the Lord' is confessed in: 'My high hand has done all these things'; and 'right hand' in: 'Exalt me with the right hand of the Lord.' For the holy one says to God: 'Yours is the arm with might, reigning and holding all things.' And it also says: 'Let your hand be strengthened, performing wonders and accomplishing great powers.'

For Peter says to God: 'Grant to your servants to speak your word with boldness, stretching out your hand for signs and wonders' (Acts 4:29). In thought, the power of the Father is not different; Christ is called these things. For if He is the Son of God and Wisdom and the Word of God and Truth, He is the right hand being lifted up by God, suspending and lifting up all, and He goes forth before your presence as mercy and truth; for no one who is to approach your face has been previously pitied and has conversed with the truth. It is possible, then, as in other places and here, that mercy and truth are not other than the Only-begotten, as in 'God sent forth His mercy and His truth.' It is not other than the Only-begotten Son of God, who is the same.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Perception of the Lord and the Vision of the Prophet
english: With the mercy and the truth of God pre-sojourning, he manifests to the minds the Father joined to him;
'For he who receives me receives the Father' (Matt 10:40), and 'We shall come, I and the Father' (John 14:23).
For being the image of the invisible God (Col 1:15), he manifests himself to the pure mind, that by being seen he may also show the Father.
But if the Son should be called the face of the Father, by being the character of his own hypostasis,
this face must go before among those who through purity of heart are able to look upon the face of God—mercy through ethical virtues and truth through knowledge of the mysteries of piety.
For since we are shown mercy according to ethical activity, and according to knowledge we approach the truth; for this reason mercy is named in many places together with truth.

If we effect power, then our horn shall be exalted in your good pleasure. For our horn was exalted by the good pleasure of God, who says, 'This is my beloved Son in whom I have been well pleased' (Matt 3:17). For He was well pleased to effect our salvation through His own Son. And because of this, he says, our horn was exalted in the good pleasure of God, since the perception of the Lord is that by which He perceives, fighting and defending those who receive this grace from Him.

And this perception belongs to the holy Israel, our king. For the king of the true Israel, seeing God, is a son; the same perception is not of the Lord. The same perception of the Lord can be as being worked by Him, and of the holy Israel as enduring it. And a holy Israel in these things is one who is sanctified in the mind to see Him. And our King, being restored by the Lord who transcends, what is the perception of our Lord the King and of the holy Israel? (Ps 88:20–23).

He who perceives a spoken word, if he only senses it, it is through hearing, if he hears the one speaking; but if he understands the things being announced, he does not perceive by hearing, but by vision of the mind he perceives the speech of the one offering it. Since God was showing things rather than merely announcing them, He speaks to His sons who are being enriched through progress and perfection, not in hearing but in vision. So also it has been written concerning Israel: 'And the people saw the voice of the Lord' (Exod 15:2). It is necessary to say, 'Heard the voice of the Lord,' but if it is said instead 'Saw the voice,' that is to say, he perceived it with the mind.

The prophets were seers of visions; for they did not say they were perceiving by sensing some things or by grasping them with the eyes, but they were striking with the mind at the beauty of intelligible things. 'You spoke in vision to your sons': 'I made help as far as possible,' saying this regarding the Savior who has come from the root of Jesse. For truly in this He set help to help all creation that is able. And the one on whom He set help is the chosen one from the people, exalted not according to divinity but according to the flesh. For concerning him it is also, 'Israel is my chosen one,' and the [people] received him...
For truly in him he set help capable of helping the whole creation.
And the mighty one upon whom he set help is the elect from the people, exalted not according to the Godhead but according to the flesh.
And concerning him is also the 'Israel my elect' (Isa 42:1); 'she received him [...].'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
